councils.

Before the Committee was a report by the
Interim Chief Executive, copies of which had been circulated to all
Members and a copy of which is attached to the signed copy of these
minutes as item 7.
 
The report before Members introduced the
emerging vision and corporate strategy for Adur & Worthing
Councils for the period 2025-2028, entitled ‘Fair, Green
& Local’. Grounded in both administration’s
priorities and shaped by community leaders through the Thriving
Together programme, the strategy established a clear direction of
travel for the coming years, with further engagement planned in the
period before finalisation in December 2025.
 
The previous strategy “Our Plan”
came to an end in October 2025 and had served the councils well
with a focus on the foundational services that residents relied
upon, establishing greater capacity for community participation,
and supporting better approaches to change and delivery through the
three principles of participation, adaptation and resilience.
 
Over the proceeding three years Adur & Worthing councils
aimed to continue to drive delivery of reliable and responsive
services and project initiatives based on the vision of delivering
“Fair, Green and Local” places. The vision was
presented within the context of ongoing and significant financial
pressures facing local government, alongside the
once-in-a-generation change of Local Government Reform (LGR). It is
designed to act as a strategic bridge, guiding the Councils through
this complex transition while continuing to deliver essential
services and long-term improvements for our communities.
 
Crucially, the vision’s direction and
priorities were a direct reflection of administration priorities
and the extensive community engagement conducted through the
‘Thriving Together’ initiative over the summer of 2025.
This process had provided a powerful public mandate for the
proposed approach, ensuring the strategy was grounded in the
expressed needs and aspirations of residents.
 
The report summarised the three core
principles of the vision—a Fairer, Greener, and more Local
future—and the five priority missions that will frame the
Councils’ work. It also introduces the draft Delivery Plan
(attached as Appendix 1), which translated those high-level
priorities into a transparent programme of tangible actions and
projects.
 
The report sought the Committee's endorsement
for the overall direction of travel and its support for a phase of
further engagement with key internal and external stakeholders as
well as Joint Overview & Scrutiny Committee. This collaborative
refinement would ensure the final vision, to be presented for
adoption in December 2025, was robust, co-owned, and ready to guide
the Councils into the future.
 
Decision:
 

1.   
That the direction of travel and the vision, principles and
missions of ‘Fair, Green & Local’ be endorsed as
outlined in this report.
 

2.   
That the proposed engagement and communication plan be supported,
as detailed in Section 5 of this report, to further develop and
refine the vision and delivery plan with key stakeholders,
including presentation of the report to the November 2025 Joint
Overview & Scrutiny Committee by the Interim Chief
Executive.
 

3.   
That a final version of ‘Fair, Green & Local’ and
Delivery Plan will be presented for formal adoption at its meeting
in December 2025 be noted.
 
 
Call In: The call-in deadline for
decisions will be 5.00pm on 21 October 2025
topline: The Joint Strategic Committee has decided to endorse the vision, principles, and missions of 'Fair, Green & Local' for Adur & Worthing Councils, setting the direction for the councils' work until 2028.

Assistant Director for Place and Economy, copies of which had been
circulated to all Members and a copy of which is attached to the

The report provided Members with an in-year
update on the performance of the Strategic Property Investment Fund
portfolio under the approved strategy. Statutory guidance placed a
duty on Local Authorities to prepare an annual Commercial Property
Investment Strategy to be approved by the full Council or
equivalent, in advance of the forthcoming financial year 2026/2027.
For 2025/2026 approval to this year's strategy was given in March
2025. This report provided an update on the recent investment
activities and position of the Strategic Property Investment Funds
(SPIFs) as of September 2025 within the approved strategy.
 
The primary objective of the Commercial
Property Investment Strategy (CPIS) was to build a balanced
portfolio generating consistent revenue for the Councils’
delivery of services for the benefit of Adur and Worthing.
 
The report provided an in-year overview of
activities in the SPIFs including measures to address energy
efficiency compliance and portfolio risks: The current overall Fund
structures and completions within the current financial year to
date; Review of economic situation and Public Works Loan Board
(PWLB) Funding criteria; Review and update of processes to support
the ongoing structured and measured approach to property income
generations and proactive risk management inherent in any property
investment; Update on mechanisms to support the ongoing retention
of a balanced portfolio with a focus on asset management and long
term capital preservation and growth.
 
Decision:
 

1.   
That it be noted that the Commercial Property Investment Strategy
Report, detailing a more in depth
analysis of funding performance to support the renewal strategy for
2026/2027, will be brought before Members in early 2026 for review
and updating;

To enter into the contract to provide stray
dog provision to Arun District Council for a further three years
from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2029.
 

The income generated from this service plays a
crucial role in offsetting the operational costs incurred by both
Adur and Worthing Councils. This financial contribution is vital in
making the provision of this essential service more viable and
sustainable in the long term, ensuring that the councils can
continue to provide effective support for stray dogs within their
respective areas. By generating revenue, the service reduces the
financial burden on local taxpayers and allows for resources to be
allocated efficiently across other council services.
 

No other options were considered necessary for
this decision. The current contract with Arun District Council has
proven to be effective and efficient in providing stray dog
services. Renewing this contract ensures continuity of service,
maintains established operational procedures, and leverages
existing expertise, thereby avoiding the disruptions and potential
increased costs associated with seeking alternative providers or
bringing the service in-house.
topline: The Assistant Director Operations & Sustainability has decided to enter into a contract to provide stray dog provision to Arun District Council for a further three years.
